name: Hamal
description: A star 20 parsecs away, 16 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 9884: radius 15.891 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 88.089 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.057) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 9884: effective temperature 4439 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.093)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.4 from 2025A&A...698A..93J; the 33 published values span log g 1.38 to 2.85, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.3% of the centre brightness

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 9884: RV -14.64 +/- 0.02 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 9884: distance 20.178 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.005), at which the luminosity and radius hold

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A star 20 parsecs away, 16 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 88 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,439 K, so 15.891 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 9884: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Hamal
quotes.card: It has the Bayer designation Alpha Arietis, which is Latinized from α Arietis and abbreviated Alpha Ari or α Ari.
quotes.introduction: This star is visible to the naked eye with an apparent visual magnitude of 2.0.
